35:1: God Almighty says: Complete thanks to the One Who is worshipped, to whomever He wills, and to whomever He wills worship... As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Those with wings, two, three, or four. Some of them said: He has two wings, some of them: three, and some of them: four. The Arabists differed about the reason for not using the dual, the thalatha, and the raba’, which is a translation of wings, and wings is indefinite. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: They were not used because they are declined from their proper forms, and that is because the dual is declined from the two, and the three from the three, and the raba’ from the four, so it was declined like ‘Umar and Zafar, as this was declined from ‘Amer to ‘Umar, and this from Zafar to Zafar. Some of them recited in that regard: I killed you, praise and unity, and left once like yesterday, the one who turned away Another of them said: It is not declined because it suggests three or four. He said: This is only used in the case of numbers. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: They are declined from definite nouns, because the definite article does not enter them, and the addition does not enter them, and the definite article would have been indefinite, and it is a translation of the indefinite noun. He said: And the same is what is in the Qur’an, like that you stand before God in pairs and singly (Saba’ 34:46), and likewise wahad and ahad, and what is similar to the declined numbers. And His saying, He increases in creation what He wills, that is His, the Blessed and Exalted, adding to the creation of this angel of wings what He wills over another, and His decreasing from another what He likes, and likewise in all of His creation, He increases in creation what He wills of it, and He decreases from creation what He wills. His is the creation and the command, and His is the power and authority. Indeed, God is over all things competent, meaning that God, the Exalted, is able to increase what He wills of that in what He wills, and to decrease what He wills of it from whomever He wills, and other than that of all things. Nothing that He wills is prevented from Him, glory be to Him, the Most High.
35:2: God Almighty says: The keys and locks of goodness are all in His hand. Whatever goodness God opens for people, no one can close it or withhold it from them, because that is His command and no one can control it. Likewise, whatever goodness He closes for them, He does not extend it to them or open it for them. No one can open it but Him, because all matters are up to Him and for Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Whatever mercy God opens for mankind means good. There is none who can withhold it so no one can stop it. And whatever He withholds, there is none who can release it after Him. And God Almighty said: There is none who can withhold it. So He made what feminine because of the mention of mercy after Him. And He said: And whatever He withholds, there is none who can release it after Him. So He made what masculine because its wording is masculine. If it were made feminine in place of masculine for the meaning, and masculine in place of feminine for the wording, it would be permissible. However, the most eloquent of speech is the feminine if it appears after what indicates its femininity, and the masculine if that does not appear. And His statement, And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, means: He is the Exalted in His vengeance upon those of His creation who took vengeance upon Him by withholding His mercy and goodness from them, the Wise in the management of His creation, and in His opening up mercy to them if opening it up is good, and in His withholding it from them if His withholding it is wisdom.
35:3: God Almighty says to the polytheists among the people of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Quraysh, O mankind, remember the favor of God which He bestowed upon you by opening for you of His goodness what He opened and by extending for you of life what He extended, and reflect and see, is there a Creator other than the Creator of the heavens and the earth, in whose hand are the keys to your provisions and their locks? He provides for you from the heaven and the earth so that you worship Him instead of Him. There is no god but Him meaning: There is no deity worthy of worship except the One who created the heavens and the earth, who is able to do all things, in whose hand are the keys to things and their treasuries, and the locks of all of that. So do not worship, O people, anything other than Him, for no one is able to benefit or harm you other than Him, so worship Him sincerely, and single Him out for divinity. How then are you turned away? He says: So which direction do you turn away from your Creator and Provider, in whose hand is your benefit and harm. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, How are you then deceived? means that a man says: He is deceiving me with such and such. I have explained the meaning of deceit and the interpretation of his statement, you are deceived, previously with supporting evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.
35:4: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: “And if these polytheists from your people deny you, O Muhammad, that should not grieve you, nor should it be a burden to you, for that was the way of their peers from the nations who disbelieved in God before them and denied the Messengers of God whom He sent to them before you. And the polytheists of your people will not be like them, and will follow their path in denying you, and will take their way.” And to God return all matters. God Almighty says: And to God is the return of your matter and their matter, so punish them if they do not return to our obedience in following you, and acknowledging your prophethood, and accepting the advice you called them to, similar to what We made permissible for their peers from the nations who denied their Messengers before you, and your savior and your followers from that, our way with those before you with our Messengers and our friends. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied, consoling his Prophet as you hear.
35:5: And His statement, O mankind, indeed the promise of God is true, is that God, the Exalted, says to the polytheists of Quraysh, who denied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O mankind, indeed God's promise to you of His punishment for your persistence in disbelieving in Him and denying His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and His warning you of the descent of His wrath upon you for that is true, so be certain of that, and hasten to face your punishment by repenting and returning to obeying God and believing in Him and His Messenger. So let not the life of this world deceive you, meaning: do not let the life you are in in this world and the leadership you have over your weak ones in it deceive you from following Muhammad and believing. And let not the Deceiver deceive you about God, meaning: do not let Satan deceive you about God, giving you false hopes, promising you false promises from God, and leading you to persist in your disbelief in God. As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning God, he said: Satan.
35:6: God Almighty says: Indeed, Satan whom I have forbidden you, O people, to be deceived by his deception of you towards God is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy meaning: so treat him among yourselves as an enemy among you, and beware of him by obeying God and seeking his deception. He has warned you against your enemy whose harm you fear for yourselves, so do not obey him and do not follow his footsteps, for he only calls his party, meaning his followers, and those who obey him to obey him and accept him, and to disbelieve in God that they may be among the companions of the Blaze meaning: that they may be among those who abide eternally in the fire of Hell which is blazing upon its inhabitants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy, for it is the right of every Muslim to be hostile to him, and his enmity is to be hostile to him through obedience to God. He only invites his party - and his party: his allies to be among the companions of the Blaze - that is, to drive them to the Fire, so this is his enmity. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze, and he said: These are his party from among mankind, he says: Those are the party of Satan, and the party: his allies whom he supports and who support him, and he recited, Indeed, my ally is God, who has sent down the Book, and He is the ally of the righteous (al-A’raf 7:196).
35:7: God Almighty says: Those who disbelieve in God and His Messenger will have a severe punishment from God, and that is the punishment of Hellfire. And His statement, and those who believe means: And those who believed in God and His Messenger, and did what God commanded them, and refrained from what He forbade them from, will have forgiveness from God for their sins and a great reward and that is Paradise. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: For them is forgiveness and a great reward, which is Paradise.
35:8: God the Almighty says: “Is he for whom Satan has made his evil deeds seem good, such as disobeying God, disbelieving in Him, and worshipping other gods and idols, so that he sees it as good, and considers its evil to be good, and thinks its ugliness to be beautiful, because Satan has made that seem attractive to him? Has your soul perished over them in regret?” The following was omitted from the statement, as the meaning of His statement, So let not your soul perish over them in regret is sufficient. And His statement, Indeed, God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills means: God lets down whomever He wills from believing in Him, following you, and believing you, so He misguides him from right guidance to the truth in that, and He guides whomever He wills: meaning: He guides whomever He wills to believe in Him, follow you, and accept you, so that you guide him to the path of right guidance. So let not your soul perish over them in regret means: Do not destroy yourself with grief over their misguidance, disbelief in God, and their denial of you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Is he to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive so he regards it as good? But God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. Qatada and al-Hasan said: Satan made them slip. So let not your soul perish over them in regret: meaning, do not let that grieve you for them, for God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, So let not your soul perish over them in regret, he said: Regrets mean sadness. And he read the statement of God, Oh, how I regretted what I neglected in my duty to God (al-Zumar 39:56), and it occurred to him, Indeed, God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills in the place of the answer, and it is the source of the answer, because the answer is what I mentioned, so it is sufficient as an answer because it indicates the answer and the meaning of the speech. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, So do not waste your soul in grief over them. The reciters of the regions, except for Abu Ja`far al-Madani, read it as So do not waste your soul with a fat-ha on the ta’ of you waste and your soul with a damma on it. Abu Ja`far read it as So do not waste your soul with a damma on the ta’ of you waste and your soul with a nasb, meaning: O Muhammad, do not waste your soul. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the reciters of the regions have said, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. And His statement, Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what they do, means that God Almighty says: O Muhammad, God is All-Knowing of what these people do, for whom Satan has made their deeds seem good, and He is recording them and repaying them with their punishment.
35:9: God Almighty says: And it is God who sends the winds that stir up the clouds for life and rain. Then We drove it to a dead land meaning: We drove it to a land barren of people, a place of land, barren with no growth or cultivation. Then We revived the land with it after its lifelessness meaning: We made fertile with the rain of that cloud the land to which We drove it after its barrenness, and We caused crops to grow in it after it had been barren. Thus is the resurrection God Almighty says: This is how God resurrects the dead after their affliction in their graves, and He revives them after their annihilation, just as We revived this land with rain after its death. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said: Abu al-Zura’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: Between the two blasts there will be whatever God wills to be, and there will be nothing of the children of Adam but that there will be some of it on the earth. He said: Then God will send water from under the Throne, semen like the semen of a man, and their bodies and flesh will grow from that, as the earth grows from the dust. Then he recited: And God is He who sends the winds, and they stir up the clouds, and We drive them to a dead land... until His saying: Thus is the resurrection. He said: Then an angel will stand with the trumpet between the heaven and the earth, and he will blow into it, and every soul will be released to its body and enter it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And God is He who sends the winds, and they stir up the clouds, he said: He sends the winds, and they drive the clouds, and God revives this dead land with this water, and thus He will resurrect it on the Day of Resurrection.
35:10: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement, Whoever desires honor, then to God belongs all honor. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Whoever desires honor by worshipping gods and idols, then to God belongs all honor. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Whoever desires honor, he says: Whoever desires honor by worshipping the gods then all honor belongs to God (An-Nisa’: 139). Others said: The meaning of this is: Whoever wants honor should be honored by obeying God. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Whoever desires honor, then to God belongs all honor, meaning: So let him seek honor through obedience to God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Whoever wants to know who the glory belongs to, then it is all for God, all of it: that is, every aspect of glory is for God. What I think is most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said: Whoever wants glory, let him seek glory through God, for glory belongs entirely to God, without any of the gods and idols that are below Him. I said: This is more correct, because the verses before this verse were about God rebuking the polytheists for their worship of idols, rebuking them, and threatening them for it. So this one also is more likely to be of the same type as urging people to abandon that, so its story was similar to its story, and it was in its context. And His statement, To Him ascends the good word, means that the Almighty says: To God ascends the servant’s remembrance of Him and his praise of Him. And righteous deeds raise it up, meaning: And the servant’s remembrance of his Lord raises it up to Him through his righteous deeds, which are working in obedience to Him, performing His obligations, and adhering to what He has commanded. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told me: Jaafar bin Awn told me, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman bin Abdullah Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mukhariq, on the authority of his father Al-Mukhariq bin Saleem, who said: Abdullah said to us: If we narrate to you a hadith, we will bring you confirmation of it from the Book of God. When a Muslim slave says: Glory be to God and His praise, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest, blessed be God, an angel takes them and places them under his wings, then he ascends with them to the heavens. No group of angels passes by them except that they seek forgiveness for the one who says them, until the Face of the Most Merciful is revived by them. Then Abdullah recited: To Him ascends good words, and righteous deeds raise them up. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Saeed Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, he said: Kaab said: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest, have a buzz around the Throne like the buzzing of bees, reminding them of their companion, and righteous knowledge is in the treasuries. Yunus told me, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab Al-Ash’ari, regarding his statement, To Him ascends good words, and righteous deeds raise them up. He said: Righteous deeds raise good words up. Ali told me, on the authority of Abu Saleh, who said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, To Him ascends good speech, and righteous action raises it. He said: Good speech is the remembrance of God, and righteous action is the performance of His obligatory duties. So whoever remembers God, the Exalted, in performing his obligatory duties, the remembrance of God is carried to him and ascends him to God. But whoever remembers God, but does not perform His obligatory duties, his speech is returned to his action, and that is more deserving of it. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahidin, regarding his statement, To Him ascends good speech, and righteous action raises it. He said: Righteous action raises good speech. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, To Him ascends good speech, and righteous action raises it. He said: Al-Hasan and Qatada said: God does not accept a word without action. Whoever speaks and does good deeds, God will accept it from him. And His statement, And those who plot evil deeds, God Almighty says: And those who commit evil deeds will have the punishment of Hell. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And those who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment. He said: These are the people of polytheism. His statement, And the plotting of those people is bound to fail, means: The work of these polytheists will fail, become null and void and disappear, because it was not for God, so it will not benefit its doer. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the plotting of those is bound to fail: that is, it will be corrupted. Yunus told me, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, And the plotting of those is bound to fail. He said: They are the people of hypocrisy. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Sahl bin Abi Aamer told us, he said: Jaafar Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, regarding His statement, And the plotting of those is doomed to fail, he said: They are the people of hypocrisy. Yunus narrated that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the plotting of those is doomed to failure, he said: It was doomed to failure, so it did not benefit them, nor did they benefit from it, and it harmed them.
35:11: God Almighty says: And God created you O people from dust meaning that He created their father Adam from dust, and made their father’s creation from him a creation for them. Then from a sperm-drop meaning: Then He created you from the sperm-drop of the man and the woman. Then He made you pairs meaning that He paired the female from the male. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And God created you from dust meaning Adam, then from a sperm-drop meaning his offspring, then He made you pairs so He paired you with one another. And His statement, And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge, God Almighty says: And no female among you, O people, conceives of pregnancy or sperm except that He knows of her pregnancy and giving birth to it, and what it is, male or female. Nothing of that is hidden from Him. And His statement, And no one is granted a long life, nor is there any reduction in his lifespan, except that it is in a book. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And no one is granted a long life, nor is there any reduction in the lifespan of another besides him, compared to the lifespan of this one who lived a long life, except that it is in a book with Him, written before his mother conceives him, and before she gives birth to him. He has accounted for all of that and known it before He created him. Nothing is added to what is written for him, nor is anything subtracted from it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And no one will be granted a long life… up to a little. He said: There is no one for whom I have decreed a long life and life except that he will reach the age that I have decreed for him, and I have decreed that for him, but he will reach the book that I have decreed for him, and nothing will be added to it. And there is no one for whom I have decreed that his life and life will be short, but he will reach the book that I have decreed for him and nothing will be added to it. So that is his statement, And no one’s life will be decreased except in a book. He said: All of that is in a book with Him. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: If someone is destined to live until he reaches old age, or to live less than that, then everyone will reach the term that has been decreed for him. All of that is in a book. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And no one is granted a long life, nor is there any reduction in his lifespan, but that it is in a book, he said: Don’t you see the people saying: A man lives a hundred years, and another dies when he is born? So this is it. So the ha’ in the statement, and his lifespan is not reduced, according to this interpretation, even though it appears to be a metaphor for the name of the first long-lived one, it is a metaphor for another name other than him. This is only good because if its owner had made it apparent, it would have appeared with the wording of the first. This is like their saying, I have a garment and half of it, but the meaning is: and half of the other. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: No one lives long, nor does his lifespan decrease due to the passing of the days of his life. This is the decrease in his lifespan, and the ha in this interpretation refers to the first one who lives long, because the meaning of the statement is: No one’s lifespan is prolonged, nor does anything of his lifespan go away, nor does it decrease except that it is written in the book of the servant of God, who has counted it and known it. Who said that? Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding this verse: And no one is granted longevity or has his lifespan cut short except in a book. He said: No one spends any of the days that were counted for him except in a book. The first of the two interpretations is the most correct in my opinion, as that is the most obvious of its two meanings, and the most similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation. His saying, Indeed, that is easy for God: God Almighty says: Confining the lives of His creation to Him is easy and simple, whether long or short, nothing of it is difficult for Him.
35:12: God Almighty says: And the two seas do not equalize, one of them is fresh and sweet, and the Euphrates is the freshest of the fresh waters, and this one is salty and bitter. He says: And the other of them is salty and bitter, and that is the green sea water, and the bitter is bitter, and it is the saltiest of the waters. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And this is salty and bitter, and bitter means bitter. And His statement, From all of them you eat tender meat, meaning: And from every sea you eat tender meat, and that fish is from their sweet Euphrates, and their salt is bitter. And you extract ornaments which you wear, meaning: Pearls and coral that you extract from the bitter salt. We have already explained before the reason for you extract ornaments, and that it is only extracted from the salt, in what has passed so that there is no need to repeat it. And you see the ships therein plowing, God Almighty says: And you see the ships in all of those seas plowing, ploughing the water with their bows, and that is their piercing it when one of them passes plowing, and it is said from it: it plowed, plowing, and plowing, and that is when it splits the water with its bows. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And from each you eat tender meat, meaning both of them, and you extract ornaments which you wear, these pearls, and you see the ships therein moving forward, meaning in it the ships coming and going with a single wind. Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And you see the ships therein moving forward, meaning: ships. And His saying, So that you may seek of His bounty, means: So that you may seek, by riding these seas in ships, for your livelihood, and to use them for your trade, and to thank God for making this subservient to you, and for what He has provided you from it of good provisions and luxurious jewelry.
35:13: God Almighty says: The night enters the day, and whatever is missing from the night He inserts into the day and adds to it, and He inserts the day into the night, and whatever is missing from the parts of the day He adds to the parts of the night, so He inserts it into them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, the increase of this is due to the decrease of this, and the decrease of this is due to the increase of this. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, meaning: It is the reduction of one from the other. And His statement, And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term, means: And He has subjected the sun and the moon to you as a blessing from Him upon you, and a mercy from Him to you, so that you may know the number of years and the reckoning, and recognize the night from the day. His saying, Everything happens for a specified term, means: Everything happens for a specific time. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term, is a known term, and a limit that it does not fall short of or exceed. His saying, That is God, your Lord, means: The One who does these actions is your God, O people, to whom worship is only appropriate, and He is God, your Lord. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, That is God, your Lord; His is the kingdom: meaning, He is the one who does this. And His saying, To Him belongs the kingdom, means that God Almighty says: To Him belongs the complete kingdom, and there is nothing but that it is in His kingdom and authority. And His statement, And those you call upon besides Him do not possess so much as a date stone, God Almighty says, “And those you worship, O people, besides your Lord, who is the attribute - mentioned in these verses, who has complete dominion, who has no dominion like Him - His attribute, “do not possess so much as a date stone,” meaning: they do not possess the husk of a date stone or anything above it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: They do not possess even a date stone, he said: It is the skin of a date pit. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, of a qatmir, meaning: the skin that is on the back of the seed. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, what they possess of even a kernel shell means: the husk of a date stone. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God from a date stone, he said: The rolling of the seed is like the inside of an egg. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, They do not possess even a single husk. The husk is the shell on top of the seed. Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of some of his companions, regarding his statement, what they possess of a single date stalk, he said: It is the stalk that is on the date. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amer told us, he said: Marra told us, on the authority of Atiyah, he said: The qatmir is the husk of the seed.
35:14: His statement, "If you call upon them, they do not hear your call. And if they heard, they would not respond to you." God Almighty says: If you call upon these gods that you worship besides God, they will not hear your call, because they are inanimate and do not understand what you say. And if they heard, they would not respond to you. He says: Even if they heard your call to them and understood from you that it is your speech, by giving them a hearing with which to hear, they would not respond to you, because they are not speaking, and not every hearer of speech is able to respond to it. God Almighty says to those who associate others with Him, the gods and idols: How can you worship besides God someone of this description, when there is no benefit to you from Him, and He has no power to harm you, and you call upon the worship of the One in whose hand is your benefit and harm, and He is the One who created you and bestowed favors upon you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “If you call upon them, they do not hear your call. And if they heard, they would not respond to you,” meaning they would not accept that from you, nor would they benefit you in it. And His statement, And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association with God, God Almighty says to the polytheists who worship idols: And on the Day of Resurrection your gods that you worship besides God will disavow having ever been partners with God in this world. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association with them, and they will not be satisfied, nor will they acknowledge it. And His statement, And none can inform you like the All-Knowing, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And none can inform you, O Muhammad, about the gods of these polytheists and what will happen to them and to their worshippers on the Day of Resurrection, from their disavowal of them and their disbelief in them, like the One who is All-Knowing of their affairs and their affairs, and that All-Knowing is God, from whom nothing, that was or will be, is hidden, glory be to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And none informs you like the All-Knowing, God is the All-Knowing that this will be one of them on the Day of Resurrection.
35:15: God Almighty says: O mankind, you are those in need and poverty before your Lord, so worship Him, and hasten to please Him, and He will enrich you from your poverty, and your needs will be fulfilled by Him. And God is the Rich from your worship of Him, and from your service, and from other things, from you and from others. The Praiseworthy means: the One praised for His blessings, for every blessing you have or others has come from Him, so to Him be praise and thanks in every situation.
35:16: God Almighty says: If He wills, He can destroy you, O people, your Lord, because He created you without any need for you. And He will bring forth a new creation. He says: And He will bring forth a creation other than you who will obey Him, follow His command, and refrain from what He has forbidden them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation: meaning, He can bring forth someone other than you.
35:17: And His statement, And that is not difficult for God, means: And your going away and bringing forth a creation other than yourselves is not difficult for God, rather that is easy and simple for Him. He says: So fear God, O people, and obey Him before He does that to you.
35:18: And His statement, And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, God Almighty says: And no sinner shall bear the sin of another. And if a heavily burdened person calls for someone to carry it, nothing of it will be borne, even if he were a close relative, God Almighty says: And if a woman burdened with sins asks someone to bear her sins and seeks that, she will not find anyone to bear any of it, even if the one she asks is a close relative, such as a father or brother. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls another to bear it, nothing of it will be borne, even if he were a close relative.” He said: There will be a burden upon him and he will not find anyone to bear any of his burden. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And if a heavily laden soul calls for its load, nothing of it will be carried is like: No soul shall bear the burden of another. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And if a heavily burdened soul calls for its load for its sins, no soul will be burdened with it, even if he were a relative: meaning, a close relative to her, he will not bear any of her sins, nor will she bear any of her sins on anyone else. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. The accusative of relative is to complete was because the meaning of the statement is: Even if the one you ask to bear her sins was a close relative to her. The feminine form of burdened is used because the statement refers to the soul, as if it was said: And if a soul burdened with sins calls for its load, and it is only said thus because the soul carries out the burden on behalf of both the male and the female, as it is said: Every soul will taste death Al Imran 3:185 - Al Anbiya 35, meaning by that: every male and female. And His statement, You only warn those who fear their Lord unseen, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You only warn, O Muhammad, those who fear God’s punishment on the Day of Resurrection without witnessing it, but because of their belief in what you have brought them and their confirmation of what you have informed them about God. These are the ones who will benefit from your warning and will take heed from your admonitions, not those whose hearts God has sealed so they do not understand. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, You only warn those who fear their Lord unseen: meaning those who fear the Fire. His statement, And establish prayer, means: They performed the obligatory prayer within its limits as God imposed it upon them. His statement, And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for the benefit of himself, means, the Most High says: And whoever purifies himself from the filth of disbelief and sins by repenting to God, believing in Him, and acting in obedience to Him, only purifies himself, for he will be rewarded thereby with the pleasure of God, attainment of His Paradise, and salvation from His punishment, which He has prepared for the disbelievers. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for the sake of himself: meaning, whoever does good, only does it for the sake of himself.
35:19: God Almighty says: The blind are not equal to the religion of God with which He sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the seeing who has seen his right path, so he followed Muhammad and believed in him, and accepted from God what He sent him with.
35:20: nor the darknesses He says: The darknesses of disbelief and the light of faith are not the same.
35:21: Nor shade It was said: Nor Paradise. Nor heat It was said: Hellfire, as if its meaning to them is: Paradise and Hellfire are not alike. And heat is like the poisonous winds, which are hot winds. Abu Ubaidah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna mentioned, on the authority of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajaj, that he used to say: The heat is at night, and the poisonous winds are during the day. As for Abu Ubaidah, he said: The heat in this place and the day is with the sun. As for al-Farra', he used to say: The heat is at night and during the day, but the poisonous winds do not occur at night, but rather during the day. In my opinion, the heat is during the night and during the day, but in this case it is more like the sun, as Abu Ubaidah said, because the shadow only occurs on a sunny day. This indicates that what is meant by heat is that which exists when there is a shadow.
35:22: And His statement, And the living are not equal to the dead, means: The living are not equal in their hearts by their belief in God and His Messenger, and their knowledge of God’s revelation, and the dead are not equal in their hearts because of the prevalence of disbelief over them, until they no longer understand God’s commands and prohibitions, and do not know guidance from misguidance. All of these are examples that God has given of the believer and faith, and the disbeliever and disbelief. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding His statement, The blind and the seeing are not alike verse, he said: It is a parable that God has given for the people of obedience and the people of disobedience, saying: The blind are not alike to darkness and heat, nor are the dead, so he is like the people of disobedience. The seeing are not alike to light, nor are the shade and the living, so he is like the people of obedience. Bishr told us, he said: Yazig told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And the blind are not equal... the verse, in creation, some are superior to others. As for the believer, he is a servant whose traces are alive, whose sight is alive, whose intention is alive, whose deeds are alive. As for the disbeliever, he is a dead servant, dead in sight, dead in heart, and dead in deeds. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “And the blind and the seeing are not alike, nor are darkness and light, nor shade and heat. Nor are the living and the dead,” he said: This is a parable that God has given. The believer has sight in God’s religion, and the disbeliever is blind, just as shade and heat are not alike, nor are the living and the dead. Likewise, this believer who sees his religion is not alike, nor this blind person. And he recited, Or he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people? Al-An’am 6:122. He said: The guidance with which God has guided him and given him light. This is a parable that God has given to this believer who sees his religion, and this blind disbeliever. So He made the believer alive, and made the disbeliever dead, dead of heart. Or he who was dead and We gave him life? Al-An’am 6:122. He said: We guided him to Islam like someone like him in darkness, blind of heart, and he is in darkness. Are these the same? The Arabists differed about the reason for the inclusion of la with the conjunction in his statement: nor darkness nor light* nor shade nor heat. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said: nor shade nor heat. So it seems that la is redundant, because if you said: Amr and Zaid are not equal in this meaning, it would not be permissible unless la is redundant. And others said: If la is not included with waw, then it is not included because it is sufficient to include it at the beginning of the speech. So if it is included, then what is meant by the speech is that each one of them is not equal to the other. So the meaning of the speech if la is repeated with waw according to the one who says this is that the blind is not equal to the seeing, and the seeing is not equal to the blind, so each one of them is not equal to the other. And His statement, Indeed, God makes hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those in the graves, says the Most High: Just as those in the graves are unable to hear the Book of God, and thus guide them to the path of righteousness, so too is he who is dead of heart among His living servants, from knowing God, and understanding His Book, His revelation, and the clarity of His proofs, unable to benefit from the sermons of God and the clarification of His arguments. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, God makes hear whomever He wills, but you cannot make hear those in the graves. Likewise, the disbeliever does not hear, nor does he benefit from what he hears.
35:23: And His statement, You are only a warner, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You are only a warner who warns these polytheists whose hearts God has sealed. Your Lord did not send you to them except to convey His message to them, and He did not charge you with a matter that you have no means to handle. As for their guidance and their acceptance of what you have brought them, that is in God's hand, not in your hand, nor in the hand of anyone else among the people. So do not waste your soul regretting them if they do not respond to you.
35:24: God, the Most High, says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, We have sent you, O Muhammad, with the truth, which is belief in God and the religious laws that He has imposed on His servants, as a bringer of good tidings, meaning: bringing good tidings of Paradise to whoever believes you and accepts from you the advice you bring from God, and a warner, warning people against your lying and rejecting the advice you bring from God. And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them, meaning: There was no nation among the nations that followed a religion but that a warner had passed among them before you, warning them of Our punishment for their disbelief in God. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them. Every nation had a messenger.
35:25: And His statement, And if they deny you, O Muhammad, those before them denied, God Almighty says, consoling His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the denial he encountered from the polytheists of his al-Nas 114:And if the polytheists of your people deny you, O Muhammad, those before them of the nations to whom their messengers came with clear proofs denied: He says: with clear proofs from God, and with scriptures, He says: and came to them with books from God. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, with clear proofs and scriptures means books, and his statement, and the illuminating book means: And the illuminating book came to them from God for whoever contemplates and ponders it, that it is the truth. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying and the illuminating Book weakens something, and it is one.
35:26: And His statement, Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My reproach? God Almighty says: Then We destroyed those who denied the message of Our Messengers and the truth of what they called them to of Our signs, and persisted in their denial. So how was My reproach? He says: So look, O Muhammad, how My change was with them and how My punishment descended upon them.
35:27: God Almighty says: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, that God sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors: He says, So We watered trees on the earth with it, and We produced thereby from those trees fruits of varying colors, some of them red, some of them black, some of them yellow, and other colors. And among the mountains are streaks of white and red. God Almighty says: And among the mountains are paths, and they are the streaks, and they are the lines that are in the mountains white, red, and black, like paths: the singular of which is a streak, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais in describing a donkey: As if his navel and back were two mounts over which a stream of rain was running. It means in essence: the black plan is on the back of the donkey. His saying, of different colors, means: the different colors of the new ones, and black crows, and that is from the introduction which means the delay, and that is because the Arabs say: he is black as a crow, if they describe him with intense blackness, and blackness here is made an attribute of crows.
35:28: And His saying, And among people, beasts, and livestock are various colors, just as among fruits and mountains are various colors, such as red, white, black, yellow, and other things. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors? “Red, green, and yellow.” And among the mountains are streaks of white, meaning white paths. And red of varying colors, meaning red and white mountains. And black crows, meaning black, meaning its color. Just as the colors of these differ, the colors of people, animals, and livestock differ likewise. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And among the mountains are streaks of white, there are streaks of white, red, and black, and so are people of different colors. Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amili told us: Marwan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement, And among the mountains are white streaks, he said: They are red and black paths. And His statement, Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: Only those who have knowledge of His ability to do whatever He wills fear God and guard against His punishment through obedience to Him, and that He does whatever He wants, because whoever knows this is certain of His punishment for his disobedience, so he fears Him and dreads Him out of fear that He will punish him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge, he said: Those who know that God is capable of all things. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge. He said: It was said: Fear is sufficient as knowledge. And His saying, Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Forgiving, God Almighty says: Indeed, God is Exalted in His vengeance against those who disbelieve in Him, and Forgiving of the sins of those who believe in Him and obey Him.
35:29: God the Almighty says: Indeed, those who recite the Book of God which He revealed to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and establish prayer means: and perform the obligatory prayer at its appointed times within its limits. He said: and establish prayer means: and establish prayer. His statement, and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly means: and give in charity from what We have given them of wealth, secretly in secret, and publicly: openly. The meaning of this is that they pay the obligatory zakat, and they also volunteer to give in charity from it after fulfilling the obligatory duty that is required of them. And His statement, they hope for a trade that will never fail means, God the Almighty says: By doing that, they hope for a trade that will never fail: that will never stagnate or perish, from their saying: the market has become barat barat” if it has stagnates and the food has become barat barat. His statement, trade is an answer to the first statement.
35:30: And His statement, That He may give them their reward in full, means: And God will give them, for their action, the reward for the deeds they did in this world. And increase them from His bounty, means: And that He may increase them, for their fulfillment, from His bounty what they are worthy of. Mutraf ibn Abdullah used to say: This is the verse of the reciters. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Amr bin Asim told us: Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, who said: When Mutraf passed by this verse, Indeed, those who recite the Book of God, he would say: This is the verse of the reciters. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Mutraf Ibn `Abdullah, that he said regarding this verse, Indeed, those who recite the Book of God...to the end of the verse. He said: This is the verse of the reciters. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Mutraf bin Abdullah used to say: This is the verse for the reciters: That He may give them their reward in full and increase them from His bounty. His saying, He is Forgiving and Appreciative, means that God is Forgiving of the sins of these people who have this characteristic, and Appreciative of their good deeds. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, He is Forgiving and Appreciative: He is Forgiving of their sins, Appreciative of their good deeds.
35:31: God Almighty says: And that which We have revealed to you of the Book O Muhammad, which is this Qur’an that God revealed to him is the truth meaning: It is the truth upon you and your nation to act upon it and follow what is in it and not any other book that was revealed to anyone other than you confirming what was before it meaning: It confirms what came before it, so it is before him from the books that I revealed to the messengers before you. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it refers to the books that came before it. And His statement, Indeed, God is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of His servants, God Almighty says: Indeed, God is All-Knowing and All-Aware of what His servants do, and All-Seeing of what is best for them in terms of management.
35:32: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the Book that God mentioned in this verse that He gave as an inheritance to those whom He chose from among His servants, and to those who are chosen from among His servants, and to those who are unjust to themselves. Some of them said: The Book is the Book that God sent down before the Criterion, and those who are chosen from among His servants are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who are unjust to themselves are the criminals among them. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then We caused the Scripture to be inherited until his statement, for the greater excellence, they are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God inherited to them every book that He revealed, so their oppressor will be forgiven, their moderate will be held to a light reckoning, and their foremost will enter Paradise without being held to account. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr bin Qais told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Isa, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Shuqaiq, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, that he said: This nation will be divided into three parts on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:a third will enter Paradise without being brought to account, a third will be brought to account with a light reckoning, and a third will come with great sins, until God says: Who are these? And He, the Blessed and Exalted, knows best. Then the angels will say: These have come with great sins, except that they did not associate anything with You. Then the Lord will say: Include these people in the breadth of My mercy. Abdullah recited this verse: Then We caused the Book to be inherited by those We have chosen of Our servants. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us: Yazid ibn Zari` told us: Awn told us: `Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal told us: Ka`b al-Ahbar told us that the one from this nation who wrongs himself, the moderate one, and the one who is foremost in good deeds, they will all be in Paradise. Have you not seen that God said, Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants... to His saying, all ungrateful. Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal, who said: I heard Kaab say: And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of God. He said: All of them are in Paradise, and he recited this verse: Gardens of Eden which they will enter (Fatir 35:33). Al-Hasan bin Arafa narrated to us, saying: Marwan bin Muawiyah Al-Fazzari narrated to us, on the authority of Awf bin Abi Jablah, saying: Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal narrated to us, saying: Kaab narrated to us that the oppressor of this nation, the moderate one, and the one who is foremost in good deeds are all in Paradise. Have you not seen that God said: Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants… until His saying: for them is the fire of Hell. And those who disbelieved will have the fire of Hell. Kaab said: So these are the people of Hell. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Awf, he said: I heard Abdullah bin Al-Harith say: Kaab said: Indeed, the one who wrongs himself, the moderate one, and the one who is foremost in good deeds from this nation: they will all be in Paradise. Have you not seen that God says: Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those We have chosen of Our servants... until he reached His saying: Gardens of Eden which they will enter. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Hamid told us, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of his father, that Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b about the words of God Almighty: Then We caused to inherit the Book those We chose of Our servants… to His words: by God’s permission. He said: Their shoulders touched, by the Lord of the Ka’bah, then they were given the bounty for their deeds. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr bin Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Sabi’in, regarding this verse: Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We chose. He said: Abu Ishaq said: As for what I heard sixty years ago, all of them are saved. He said: Amr told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said: It is a nation that is shown mercy. The oppressor is forgiven, the moderate is in Paradise with God, and the one who is foremost in good deeds is in the highest ranks with God. Others said: The book that these people inherited is the testimony that there is no god but God, and the chosen ones are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the one among them who is unjust to himself is the hypocrite, and he is in Hell, and the moderate one and the one who is foremost in good deeds is in Paradise. Who said that? Abu Ammar Al-Hussein bin Harith Al-Marwazi told us: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Hussein bin Waqid, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abdullah: And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds. He said: Two will be in Paradise, and one will be in Hell. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those We chose of Our servants... to the end of the verse. He said: He divided the people of faith into three levels, like His statement, And the companions of the left are from the companions of the left (al-Waqi’ah 56:41), And the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? (al-Waqi’ah 56:27), “And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near” (al-Waqi’ah 56:10-11). So they are on this example. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate... the verse. He said: Two will be in Paradise, and one will be in Hell. It is like the one in al-Waqi’ah 56:And the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right? (al-Waqi’ah 56:27), And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? (al-Waqi’ah 56:41), And the foremost will be the foremost. (al-Waqi’ah 56:10). Sahl ibn Musa told us: Abd al-Majid told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants, and among them is he who wrongs himself, he said, They are the companions of the left, “And among them is he who is moderate,” he said, They are the companions of the right, “And among them is he who is foremost in good deeds,” he said, They are the foremost among all people. Al-Hasan bin Arafa narrated to us: Marwan bin Muawiyah narrated to us: Aouf said: Al-Hasan said: As for the one who is unjust to himself, he is the hypocrite. This is omitted. As for the moderate and the one who is foremost in good deeds, they are the companions of Paradise. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Awf, he said: Al-Hasan said: The one who is unjust to himself is the hypocrite. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants, “the testimony that there is no god but God,” and among them is he who wrongs himself, this is the hypocrite according to Qatada and al-Hasan. And among them is he who is moderate, he said: This is the companion of the right. And among them is he who is foremost in good deeds, he said: This is the one brought near. Qatada said: People had three levels in this world, three levels at death, and three levels in the Hereafter. As for this world, they were: a believer, a hypocrite, and a polytheist. As for at death, God said, “But if he should be of those brought near, * Then will be comfort and basil and a Garden of Delight. But if he should be of the companions of the right, * Then, peace be upon you from the companions of the right. But if he should be of the deniers and those who have gone astray, * Then will be an accommodation of scalding water * And burning in Hellfire.” Al-Waqi’ah 58:88-94 As for the Hereafter, they were three pairs: (Then the companions of the right - who are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left - who are the companions of the left? And the foremost - the foremost. Those are the ones nearest to God.) (al-Waqi’ah 56:8-11). Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants, and among them is he who wrongs himself, he said: They are the companions of the left. And among them is he who is moderate, he said: The companions of the right. And among them is he who is foremost in good deeds, he said: They are the foremost among all people. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants, and among them is he who wrongs himself He said: This was omitted, And among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of God He said: This one was foremost in good deeds, and this one is moderate in his footsteps. The most correct interpretation of this is the one that says: What is meant by His statement, Then We caused to inherit the Book those We chose of Our servants, is the books that were revealed before the Criterion. If someone were to say: How can this be the meaning, while the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only recite their book, and only act according to the rulings and laws contained therein? It would be said: The meaning of this is different from what you have suggested. Rather, it means: Then We caused faith in the book to be inherited by those We have chosen. Among them are those who believe in every book that God sent down from the heaven before their book and act according to it. This is because every book sent down from the heaven before the Criterion commands acting according to the Criterion when it is revealed, and following the one who brought it. This is the action of the one who acknowledges Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and what he brought, and acts according to what he called for in the Qur’an and in the other books that were sent down before it. Rather, it was said: What is meant by His statement, Then We caused the Scripture to be inherited is the Scriptures that we mentioned, because God, the Most High, said to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, And that which We have revealed to you of the Scripture is the truth, confirming what was before it. Then He followed that with His statement, Then We caused the Scripture to be inherited by those We have chosen. So it was known, since the meaning of inheritance is the transfer of a meaning from one people to another, and there was no nation at the time of our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to whom a Scripture was transferred from a people before them other than his nation, that this is its meaning. And since that is the case, it is clear that the chosen ones from among His servants are the believers of His nation. As for the one who wrongs himself, then being among the people of sins and transgressions that are less than hypocrisy and polytheism is more similar to the meaning of the verse in my opinion than being a hypocrite or a disbeliever. This is because God, the Most High, followed this verse with His statement, Gardens of Eden which they will enter, so entering Paradise is general for all three categories. If someone says: His statement, They will enter it, only refers to the moderate and the foremost. It is said to him: What is your proof that this is the case, whether from the report or reason? If he says: The established proof is that the oppressor of this nation will enter Hellfire, and if none of these three categories entered Hellfire, then there would be no threat for the people of faith. It is said: The verse does not state that they will not enter Hellfire, but rather it contains information from God, the Most High, that they will enter the Gardens of Eden. It is possible that the oppressor will enter it for himself after God punished him for the sins he committed in this world, and his oppression of himself therein with Hellfire, or with whatever punishment He wills, then He will admit him to Paradise, and he will be among those who are covered by the information of God, the Most High, in His statement, Gardens of Eden which they will enter. It has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner similar to what we have mentioned in this regard, even though there is some doubt about its chains of transmission, along with the evidence of the Book for its authenticity in the manner that I have explained. Mentioning the narration that was reported about that: Muhammad bin Bashar narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: Abu Thabit mentioned that he entered the mosque, sat next to Abu Al-Darda’, and said: O God, comfort my loneliness, have mercy on my estrangement, and make a righteous companion easy for me. Abu Al-Darda’ said: If you are truthful, then I am happier with him than you. I will tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that I have not told since I heard him mention this verse: “Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds.” As for the one who is foremost in good deeds, he will enter it without being held to account. As for the moderate, he will be held to an easy account. As for the one who wrongs himself, grief and sadness will be afflicted in that place. That is His saying: Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow (Fatir 35:34). Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated: Muhammad ibn Ja’far narrated: Shu’bah narrated from Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah that he heard a man from Thaqeef narrating from a man from Kinanah, from Abu Sa’eed Al-Khudri, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said concerning this verse: “Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God’s permission.” He said: All of these are of one status, and all of them are in Paradise. What He meant by His statement, those We have chosen of Our servants is those whom We have selected for Our obedience and chosen. And His statement, among them is he who wrongs himself means: Among those whom We have chosen of Our servants are those who wrong themselves by committing sins, committing transgressions, and perpetrating indecencies. And among them is he who is moderate, who is not excessive in obeying his Lord, and not striving in what he is required to do in serving his Lord, so that his actions in that are moderate. And among them is he who is foremost in good deeds, who is the prominent one who has preceded the striving in serving His Lord, and the performance of his duties, so he preceded them with righteous deeds, which are the good deeds about which God Almighty said, by God’s permission, meaning: by God’s granting him success in that. And His statement, That is the great bounty, God Almighty says: The precedence of this forerunner over those who preceded him in good deeds by God’s permission is the great bounty by which He favored those who were falling short of their station in obeying God, from the moderate and the unjust to themselves.
35:33: God Almighty says: Gardens of residence which they will enter, those whom We have given as inheritance to, whom We have chosen from among Our servants on the Day of Resurrection. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold. “They will wear bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein will be silk.” He says: And their clothing in Paradise will be silk. And His statement, And they said, ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow.’ The people of interpretation differed regarding the sorrow that these people praised God for removing from them. Some of them said: It was the sorrow that they were in before entering Paradise due to fear of Hell, as they were afraid that they would enter it. Who said that? Qatada bin Saeed bin Qatada Al-Sadusi told me, he said: Muadh bin Hisham, the companion of Al-Dastawai, told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow, he said: The sorrow of the Fire. Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yahya ibn al-Mukhtar, on the authority of al-Hasan (And when the ignorant address them, they say, “Peace” (al-Furqan 25:63) He said: The believers are a people who are humbled. By God, their ears, eyes, and limbs are humbled, to the point that the ignorant person thinks they are sick, but there is no sickness among the people. They are the healthiest of hearts, but fear has entered them in a way that has not entered others, and their knowledge of the Hereafter has prevented them from this world.
35:34: They said: Praise be to God who has removed our sorrow. And sorrow, by God, did not make them sad the sorrow of this world, nor did they feel great in their souls what they had asked for in Paradise. Rather, the fear of Hellfire made them cry. And whoever does not seek comfort in God's comfort cuts himself off from this world with regrets. And whoever does not see God's blessing upon him except in food or drink, his knowledge has become small, and his punishment is present. Others said: It means death. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah, regarding his statement, Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow, he said: death. Others said: It means the sadness of bread. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Hafs, meaning Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar, who said: When God brought the people of Paradise into Paradise, they said, Praise be to God who has removed from us sorrow. He said: The sorrow of bread. Others said: What he meant by that was: sadness from the fatigue they were in in this world. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And they said, ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow.’ He said: They were working and toiling in this world, while they were in fear or sorrow. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that is the sadness that the oppressor will feel for himself on the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: Abu Thabit mentioned that Abu Al-Darda’ said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be afflicted in that place with grief and sadness, and that is his saying: ‘Praise be to God who has removed sadness from us.’” The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty mentioned about these people whom He honored with what He honored them with, that they said when they entered Paradise, Praise be to God who has taken away from us sorrow. The fear of entering Hell is from sorrow, the fear of death is from sorrow, and the fear of needing food is from sorrow. God did not specify when He mentioned about them that they praised Him for taking away sorrow from them in one way rather than another, rather He mentioned about them that they included all types of sorrow by saying that. And likewise, because whoever enters Paradise has no sorrow after that, so He praised them for taking away from them all meanings of sorrow. And His statement, Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative, the Most High says, informing about what was said by these categories of people whom He informed that He chose from among His servants when they entered Paradise: Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving of the sins of His servants who repented from their sins, and concealed them by His pardoning them for them, and Appreciative of them for their obedience to Him, and the righteous deeds they presented in this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative, for their good deeds. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shamir: Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative. He forgave them for their sins and was grateful for what they did.
35:35: God Almighty says, informing us of what was said by those who were admitted to Paradise: Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative * Who has settled us in the home of permanence. That is, our Lord who has settled us in this home, meaning Paradise. So the home of permanence is the home of residence from which there is no moving or shifting. If the mim is pronounced with a damma in al-maqama, then it is from iqama, and if it is pronounced with a fatha, then it is from al-majlis, or the place in which one stays. The poet said: Two days: one day of gatherings and clubs, and one day of marching to the enemies for retribution. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He who has settled us in the home of permanence out of His bounty they stayed and did not move. His saying, No fatigue or pain will touch us therein, means: No weariness or exhaustion will touch us therein, “nor will fatigue or exhaustion touch us therein,” meaning by weariness: toil and fatigue. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that?
