Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Musa bin Umair told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Therein we shall not be touched by fatigue, nor shall we be touched by weariness, he said: Laghoub means toil. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, No fatigue will touch us therein means pain.
35:36: God Almighty says, And those who disbelieve in God and His Messenger for them is the fire of Hell. He says: For them is the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. Notice that they will not be in Paradise or its pleasures. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “For them is the fire of Hell. They will not be decreed” by death so that they die, because if they died they would be at rest. Nor will its punishment be lightened for them. He says: Nor will the punishment of the fire of Hell be lightened for them by their death, so that it will be lightened for them. As Mutraf bin Abdullah Al-Dhabi told me, he said: Abu Qutaybah told us, he said: Abu Hilal Al-Rasibi told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Al-Sawda, he said: The poor people of Hell will not die. If they died, they would find rest. Uqbah narrated to me on the authority of Sinan al-Qazzaz, who said: Ghassan ibn Mudar narrated to us, who said: Saeed ibn Yazid narrated to us, and Yaqub narrated to me, who said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Yazid, and Suwar ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Abu Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for the people of Hell, who are its people, they will neither die in it nor live, but people, or something like that, will be afflicted by the Fire because of their sins, or he said: because of their transgressions, and He will cause them to die a great death until they have become charcoal, and permission will be given for intercession, and they will be brought in groups, and spread among the people of Paradise. He said: O people of Paradise, pour out your blessings upon them so that they may grow as a seed grows in the silt of a torrent. A man from the people then said: It is as if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been in the desert.” If someone says: How is it said, And their punishment will not be lightened when it was said in another place: Every time it subsides, We will increase their blazing fire (al-Isra’ 17:97), it is said that the meaning of that is: And their punishment will not be lightened from this type of punishment. And His statement, Thus do We reward every ungrateful person, God Almighty says: Thus will He reward every ungrateful person for the blessings of his Lord on the Day of Resurrection, by admitting them into the fire of Hell for the sins they committed in this world.
35:37: And His statement, And they will cry out therein, 'Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we were doing.' God Almighty says: These disbelievers are crying out and making a noise in the Fire, saying, Our Lord, take us out; we will do righteousness, meaning, we will do Your obedience, other than what we were doing before, disobeying You. And His statement, they will cry out, is a plural of screaming. Its ta' was changed to a ta' because its articulation is close to the sad because it is heavy. And His statement, Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would remember to remember therein? The people of interpretation differed regarding the amount of that, and some of them said: That is forty years. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khaitham told us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Life is for which God has excused the son of Adam, Have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember?: forty years. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, that he used to say: When one of you reaches the age of forty, let him be on his guard against God. Others said: Rather, it is sixty years. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Khaitham, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember therein? He said: Sixty years. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard Abdullah bin Othman bin Khaitham, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The age in which God excuses the son of Adam is sixty years. Ali bin Shuaib told us: Muhammad bin Ismail bin Abi Kadik told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Al-Fadl, on the authority of Abu Husayn Al-Makki, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be called: Where are the sixty-year-olds? This is the age of which God said: ‘Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember, and a warner came to you?’” Ahmad bin Al-Faraj Al-Himsi told me: Baqiyah bin Al-Walid told us: Mutraf bin Mazen Al-Kinani told us: Muammar bin Rashid told us: I heard Muhammad bin Abdul-Rahman Al-Ghifari say: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has excused the one who is sixty years old or seventy. Abu Saleh Al-Fazari told us: Muhammad bin Suwar told us: Yaqub bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Abd Al-Qari Al-Iskandari told us: Abu Hazim told us, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever God gives a life of sixty years has been excused for his life. Muhammad bin Suwar told us: Asad bin Hamid told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Tarif, on the authority of Al-Asbagh bin Nabatah, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement, Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember therein, and a warner had come to you? He said: The lifespan that God gave you is sixty years. The two interpretations of the verse are more similar to those of the two statements, since the report we mentioned from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a report in whose chain of transmission there is some that must be verified in its transmission. The statement of the one who said that was forty years, because at forty a person’s mind and understanding reach their peak, and what comes before and after that is less than its perfection at forty. And his saying, And a warner has come to you, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the warner. Some of them said: He meant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And a warner has come to you, he said: The warner is the Prophet. And he recited, This is a warner among the first warners (al-Najm 53:56). It was said that he meant gray hair by it. So the interpretation of the statement is: Did We not grant you, O group of polytheists from Quraysh, a life of years, such that those of understanding and reason would remember, and those of them who were admonished would take heed, and those of them who repented would repent, and a warner would come to you from God warning you of what you are in today of God’s punishment, but you did not remember God’s admonitions, and you did not accept from God’s warner who came to you what he brought you from your Lord? God Almighty says: Then taste the fire of the torment of Hell which you have been exposed to, O disbelievers in God. For there is no helper for the wrongdoers. He says: So there is no helper for the disbelievers who wronged themselves and earned God’s wrath by their disbelief in God in this world to aid them from God and rescue them from His punishment.
35:38: And His statement, Indeed, God is Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth, God Almighty says: Indeed, God is Knower of what you conceal, O people, within yourselves and what you conceal, and what you do not conceal and do not intend of what you will intend, and what is hidden from your sight in the heavens and the earth. So fear Him, lest He should see you while you conceal within yourselves doubts about the Oneness of God, or about the prophethood of Muhammad, other than what you reveal with your tongues. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
35:39: God Almighty says: God is He who made you, O people, successors on the earth after Aad and Thamud, and those nations who passed before you, and made you succeed them in their homes and dwellings. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, It is He who made you successors on the earth, nation after nation, and century after century. And His statement, But whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief, God Almighty says: Whoever among you, O people, disbelieves in God, then upon himself is the harm of his disbelief. He does not harm anyone but himself, because he is the one who is punished for it and no one else. And His statement, And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers in the sight of their Lord except in hatred, God Almighty says: And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers in the sight of their Lord except in distance from the mercy of God. And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers except in loss, He says: And their disbelief in God does not increase the disbelievers except in destruction.
35:40: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your al-Nas 114:‘Have you seen, O people, your partners whom you call upon besides God? Show me what they have created on the earth.’” He says: Show me what they have created on the earth. Or do they have a share in the heavens? He says: Or do your partners have a share with God in the heavens, if they have not created anything on the earth? Or have We given them a Book from which they have clear evidence? He says: Or have We given these polytheists a Book which We sent down to them from the heavens, that they should associate with God idols and statues, so they have clear evidence from it, so they have proof of what I have commanded them to do regarding associating partners with Me. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Say, ‘Have you seen your partners whom you invoke besides God? Show me what they have created on the earth.’ Nothing, by God, they created from it. Or do they have a share in the heavens? “No, by God, they have no share in them.” Or have We given them a book from which they are on clear evidence? He says, Or have We given them a book so that it commands them to associate. And His statement, Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion, that is, some of them saying to one another, We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to God (al-Zumar 39:3), is a deception and delusion from some of them to one another. Their gods only draw them closer to the Fire and distance them from God and His mercy.
35:41: God Almighty says: Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they move from their places. And if they were to move means: Even if they were to move. If anyone were to hold them back after Him means: No one would hold them back other than Him. The word if in the phrase and if they were to move is used in place of if because they are answered with the same answer, so they are similar in meaning. Similar to that is His statement: And if We sent a wind and they saw it yellow, they would continue to disbelieve after that Ar-Rum 30:51 meaning: Even if We sent a wind. And as He said: And if you were to bring to those who were given the Scripture Ar-Baqarah 2:145 meaning: If you were to bring. We have already explained that in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist from their places. Ibn Bashar narrated: Abdur-Rahman narrated: Sufyan narrated: Al-A'mash narrated: Abu Wa'il said: A man came to Abdullah and said: Where did you come from? He said: From Ash-Sham. He said: Whom did you meet? He said: I met Ka'b. He said: What did Ka'b tell you? He said: He told me that the heavens revolve around the shoulder of an angel. He said: Did you believe him or disbelieve him? He said: I neither believed him nor disbelieved him. He said: I would have liked to have been ransomed from your journey to him by your mount and its saddle. Ka'b lied! God says: "Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist. And if they should cease, no one could hold them back after Him." Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Jundub Al-Bajali went to Ka’b Al-Ahbar, came to him and then returned. Abdullah said to him: Tell us what he told you. He said: He told me that the sky is on a pole like the pole of a millstone, and the pole is a pillar on the shoulder of an angel. Abdullah said: I wish you had redeemed your journey with a mount like yours. Then he said: Judaism does not insinuate itself in the heart of a servant so that it almost leaves him. Then he said: Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist. It is enough for them to cease to exist that they revolve. And His statement, Indeed, He was Forbearing and Forgiving, means that God Almighty says: Indeed, God was Forbearing toward those of His creation who associated partners with Him and disbelieved in Him, by not hastening His punishment for them, and Forgiving of the sins of those of them who repented and turned to faith in Him and doing what pleases Him.
35:42: God Almighty says: And these polytheists swore by God with their most vehement oaths: meaning: the most vehement oaths, so they exaggerated in them, that if a warner came to them from God to warn them of God’s punishment, they would surely be better guided than any of the nations meaning: they would surely be more treading the path of truth, and more accepting of what the warner from God would bring them, than any of the nations created before them. Then when there came to them a warner meaning by warner: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says: When Muhammad came to them to warn them of God’s punishment for their disbelief. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, So when a warner came to them, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. His statement, It only increased their aversion, means: The coming of the warner only increased their belief in God, following the truth, and following the right path, in aversion and flight.
35:43: His statement, arrogance on earth, means: They went forth arrogantly on earth and with a bad trick, as they prevented the weak from following him despite their disbelief in him. And the trick here is polytheism. And Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And the plotting of the evil, which is polytheism, and the plotting was attributed to the evil, and the evil is from the description of the plot, as it was said: Indeed, this is the certain truth (al-Waqi’ah 56:95). And it was said that that is in the reading of Abdullah and an evil plot, and in that is the confirmation of the statement that the evil in meaning is from the description of the plot, and the readers of the regions other than Al-A’mash and Hamzah read that with a moving hamzah in the genitive case. And Al-A’mash and Hamzah read that with a hamzah and a sukun on the hamzah, based on their reasoning that when the vowels are many in that, it becomes heavy, so they sukun the hamzah, as the poet said: If they are crooked, I say they are the companions of the people The letter Baa is silent due to the many vowels. The correct reading is what the reciters of the regions do, which is to move the hamza to the khafd. It is not permissible in the Qur’an to read with everything that is permissible in Arabic, because the reading is only what the past imams read, and what the predecessors came with in the manner that they took from those before them. His statement, And the evil plot will not encompass except its own people, means: And the evil plot will not befall except its own people, meaning those who plot it. Rather, he meant that the evil of that plot that these polytheists plotted will not befall except them. Qatada said about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And evil plotting does not encompass except its own people, which is polytheism. And His statement, Do they then await anything but the way of the former peoples? God Almighty says: Do these polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, await anything but the way God will treat them in this worldly life, for their disbelief in Him, the painful punishment? He says: Do these people await anything but that I should bring upon them from My vengeance, for their associating partners with Me and denying My Messenger, the same as I brought upon those nations like them before them? As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then you will not find any change in the way of God, meaning the punishment of the people of old. You will not find any change in the way of God, he said: You will not find, O Muhammad, any change in the way of God. And His statement, And you will not find any change in the way of God, means: And you will not find any alteration in the way of God in His creation. He says: He will not change that, nor alter it, because there is no turning back from His judgment.
35:44: God Almighty says: Did not these polytheists, O Muhammad, travel through the land whose people We destroyed because of their disbelief in Us and their denial of Our Messengers? They were merchants who took the road to Ash-Sham, so they could see how was the end of those before them, of the nations they used to pass through. Did We not destroy them and destroy their dwellings and make them an example for those after them, so that they would learn from them and be deterred from what they were doing of worshipping gods by associating partners with God, and know that the One who did to those what He did, and they were stronger than them in strength, would not be unable to do to them what He did to those, by hastening the punishment and torment for them. And in a manner similar to what we said about His statement, And they were stronger than them in strength, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they were stronger than them informs you that he gave the people what he did not give you. And His statement, And nothing in the heavens or on the earth could escape God, means, “And these polytheists who worship idols and deny Muhammad will never escape Us, outrunning Us on earth, if We wish to destroy them, because nothing He desires in the heavens or on the earth could escape God. And these polytheists will never be able to penetrate beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth.” And His statement, Indeed, He is All-Knowing and All-Powerful, means, “Indeed, God is All-Knowing of His creation and what will happen, and who among them deserves to be hastened to punish, and who among them is returning from his misguidance and returning to guidance. He is Able to take revenge on whomever He wills among them, and to guide whomever He wills among them to faith.”
35:45: God Almighty says: And if God were to punish people for their sins and transgressions, and the wrongdoings they committed, He would not leave on the earth’s surface a single creature to creep upon. But He defers them for a specified term. He says: But He defers their punishment and their being held accountable for what they have earned for a term known to Him, limited, before which they will not fall short, nor will they exceed it if they reach it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And if God were to punish people for what they have earned, He would not leave on the surface of the earth a single creature except what Noah carried in the ship. And His statement, So when their term comes, then indeed, God is ever, over His servants, Seeing. God Almighty says: So when the term of their punishment comes, then God is ever, over His servants, Seeing who among them deserves to be punished, who deserves honor, who among them was obedient to Him in this world, and who was a polytheist in it. None of them is hidden from Him, and nothing of their affair is hidden from Him.
